domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: A patient with diffuse skin thickening requires pre-op evaluation. Which three organ systems must be specifically assessed beyond skin?
answer: Kidneys, heart, and lungs must be evaluated for systemic involvement.
rationale: Systemic sclerosis causes multiorgan fibrosis; renal crisis, PAH, pericardial disease, and ILD each carry independent mortality.

domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: A scleroderma patient develops sudden hypertension and rising creatinine. What treatment changes 1-year survival from <15% to >85%?
answer: ACE inhibitors; they interrupt renin-angiotensin activation driving scleroderma renal crisis.
rationale: Renal crisis involves renin release from ischemic vessels; ACE inhibitors blunt this cascade and dramatically improve survival.

domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: What percentage of systemic sclerosis patients have ANAs, and name three more specific autoantibodies?
answer: ANAs >90%; anti-centromere, anti-Scl-70, and anti-RNA polymerase III (found in up to 70%).
rationale: These specific antibodies correlate with clinical subtype; anti-RNA pol III predicts renal crisis, anti-centromere predicts limited disease with PAH.

domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: A scleroderma patient has dyspnea and mean PAP 27 mmHg with normal wedge on right heart cath. What diagnosis is confirmed?
answer: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH): mean PAP >=25 mmHg + normal PCWP.
rationale: Right heart catheterization is the gold standard; normal PCWP excludes left heart failure as the cause of elevated PAP.

domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: Which esophageal motility disorder is scleroderma most commonly associated with, and what anesthetic aspiration risk does it create?
answer: Hypomotility/aperistalsis causing GERD; increased aspiration risk at induction requires RSI or awake intubation.
rationale: Loss of lower esophageal sphincter tone plus dysmotility causes chronic GERD, increasing full-stomach risk.
confusable_with: Achalasia (high LES pressure, not absent tone)

domain: Internal medicine: rheumatology, immunology & allergy (gout & crystal arthropathy, SLE, RA, vasculitides, anaphylaxis & angioedema, drug reactions)
stem: Which racial group with scleroderma has earlier onset, more severe disease, and higher rates of ILD and renal crisis?
rationale: Racial disparities reflect genetic and access factors; African-Americans are disproportionately affected by severe manifestations and require closer monitoring.

enabling_conditions: Female sex 3-4:1, age 30-50, HLA susceptibility, silica/organic solvent exposure
pathophysiology: Triad: autoimmunity + vasculopathy + fibrosis; T-cell activation, TGF-beta, endothelial injury precedes fibrosis
time_course: Slow years-long progression; Raynaud's precedes skin changes; diffuse form progresses faster
key_features: Skin thickening hands/face, Raynaud's, esophageal dysmotility, PAH, ILD, renal crisis (HTN + AKI)
consequence_if_missed: Scleroderma renal crisis without ACE inhibitor: <15% 1-year survival; undiagnosed PAH leads to right heart failure
